lesson.text: Quick memory: where do you change trains on a metro map? (Where two lines meet.) Today: a journey on your own, a map's grid and a compass bearing.
Plan it: your start, the change, your end. Trains are signed by the last station they go to, so take the one towards the end of the line past your stop.
Wait behind the yellow line; let people off first; mind the gap. Separated from your group? Stay put and ask the staff at a help point.
A map's key explains its symbols. Grid squares: read along the bottom first, then up the side: along the corridor, then up the stairs.
A bearing: set the degrees on the dial at the arrow, turn until the red needle sits in its outline, then walk where the arrow points. 90 degrees is east.
Try it in the world: open the practice metro and park, on the Big track.
